1	---
2	title: "The cursor in a recording"
3	description: "Choose whether the pointer is kept out of a screen recording for Frame Job to draw, or drawn into the movie by macOS, and how clicks are shown."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	A screen recording can keep the pointer out of the movie, so Frame Job draws it on the clip and you can restyle it later, or have macOS draw it into the picture for good. You choose before you record, because the choice is part of the movie.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
12	  keys="⌥⌘N"
13	  where={['New Recording panel ▸ Cursor', 'New Recording panel ▸ Show Clicks']}
14	  tools="record_screen"
15	/>
16	
17	## Choose Separate or In the picture
18	
19	Set **Cursor** on the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/).
20	
21	| | **Separate** | **In the picture** |
22	| --- | --- | --- |
23	| The pointer | Kept out of the movie. Frame Job draws it on the clip. | Drawn into the movie by macOS. |
24	| Restyle it later | Yes, in the clip's **Cursor** section. | No. It can't be changed or removed. |
25	| **Show Clicks** | Click ripples, drawn by Frame Job. | A ring drawn into the movie. |
26	| The **Cursor** section | Appears on the clip. | Doesn't appear. |
27	| Cursor file | Written | Written |
28	
29	**Separate** is the default for every screen source: displays, windows and picked windows. Your choice is remembered, and once you've made one it holds for every source.
30	
31	Both write a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) beside the movie, so [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/), [shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/) and [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/) work either way.
32	
33	With **Separate**, the pointer appears wherever Frame Job draws the clip, in the preview and in every export. The movie file on its own has no pointer, so opened in another app it shows none.
34	
35	**Cursor** is greyed out, keeping its value, with **Camera** or **Microphone Only** as the source, and while a recording is under way.
36	
37	## Show clicks
38	
39	**Show Clicks** marks each mouse click. It's off by default, and greyed out with **Camera** or **Microphone Only**.
40	
41	- **With In the picture**, macOS draws a ring around each click into the movie. It can't be removed afterwards.
42	- **With Separate**, nothing is drawn into the movie. Frame Job draws the ripples from the cursor file, and you can edit them afterwards.
43	
44	## What a Separate recording lands with
45	
46	The clip gets a **Cursor** section on the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab, with the pointer drawn as recorded. See [Style the recorded cursor](/recording/cursor-settings/) for what you can change there.
47	
48	With **Show Clicks** on as well, the clips land with **Clicks** set to **Ripple**, in the same undo step as the recording. In a new project where that's the only other change, the undo step is called **Cursor Clicks**. Undoing it takes the ripples off and keeps the pointer.
49	
50	Nothing else is set. **Polish**, in the same section, is one click away.
51	
52	## What an In the picture recording lands with
53	
54	The pointer is in the movie and the cursor file says so, so the clip shows no **Cursor** section and nothing is drawn twice.
55	
56	## Good to know
57	
58	If a **Separate** stretch's cursor file couldn't be written, that stretch has no pointer at all: it isn't in the movie and there's nothing to draw it from. It gets no ripples either. The panel's note says so, with "The pointer is not in the movie either: it was recorded Separate."
59

1:---
2:title: "Record with record_screen"
3:description: "How an agent records the screen, a camera or a voice-over for a set time and lands it in a project: every argument, answer and refusal."
4:---
5:
6:import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7:
8:`record_screen` is **File ▸ New Recording…** without the panel. An agent says how many seconds to record, the call runs for that long, and the recording lands in the project the way one made with the panel does. There's no countdown, and the tool never asks 
9:
10:<AtAGlance
11:  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
12:  tools="record_screen"
13:  needs={[
14:    'Screen Recording permission, for a screen recording',
15:    'Microphone, Camera or Input Monitoring, only when the call uses them',
16:    'A person has to give each permission first',
17:  ]}
18:/>
19:
20:## Record the screen
21:
22:The smallest call names only `seconds`:
23:
24:```json
25:{ "seconds": 30 }
26:```
27:
28:That records the main display for 30 seconds with its system sound, leaves Frame Job's own windows out of the picture, and lands the movie at the playhead of the front project. A recording then goes through these stages:
29:
30:- **It starts at once.** There's no countdown and no panel.
31:- **It writes to disk.** The file goes to `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings`, named for example `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.mov`, and it's never stored inside the project. A name that's already taken gets ` (2)`, ` (3)` and so on.
32:- **It lands.** The movie becomes ordinary media, and a clip goes at the playhead on the front track of whatever is open, a [nest](/mcp/nests/) included. When that track has no room there, Frame Job adds a new track in front of everything. This is one undo 
33:- **It answers.** The call returns once the recording is finished, imported and placed. See [What it answers](#what-it-answers).
34:
35:With no project open, the recording opens as a new untitled project instead, and `landed` reads `new_project`. Its canvas takes the movie's size and `rate`. Later calls address that project with `project` set to the recording's path, which is the path `get_
36:
37:Only one recording runs at a time, whoever started it. A second one is refused with "A recording is already in progress."
38:
39::::note
40:The built-in [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) can't call `record_screen`. Recording stays with a person at the Record button, or an agent connected from outside.
41::::
42:
43:[Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) has the landing in full, and it's the same for both.
44:
45:## Choose a source
46:
47:`source` says what's recorded.
48:
49:| `source` | What it records | Files |
50:| --- | --- | --- |
51:| `screen` | A display or a window. The default. | `Screen Recording <date> at <time>.mov` |
52:| `voice_over` | The default microphone alone, with no picture. | `Voice-over <date> at <time>.m4a` |
53:| `camera` | A camera alone, with no screen. | `Camera Recording <date> at <time>.mov` |
54:
55:An argument the source can't use is refused by name, not ignored. A JSON null counts as not given. This is what each source takes:
56:
57:| Argument | `screen` | `voice_over` | `camera` |
58:| --- | --- | --- | --- |
59:| `seconds`, `project`, `path`, `place`, `enhance` | Yes | Yes | Yes |
60:| `microphone` | Yes | Implied, and `false` is refused | Yes |
61:| `rate` | Yes | Yes, for a new project's canvas | Refused |
62:| `camera`, `camera_format` | Yes, [beside the screen](#record-a-camera-beside-the-screen) | Refused | Yes |
63:| `camera_layout`, `camera_cutout` | Yes, with `camera` | Refused | Refused |
64:| `display`, `window`, `size`, `include_framejob_windows` | Yes | Refused | Refused |
65:| `system_audio`, `show_clicks`, `cursor`, `keys` | Yes | Refused | Refused |
66:| `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing` | Yes | Refused | Refused |
67:
68:## The arguments
69:
70:Only `seconds` is required. The sections further down cover the arguments for [voice-overs](#record-a-voice-over), [cameras](#record-a-camera-alone) and the [steps after landing](#run-steps-after-it-lands).
71:
72:### Length and source
73:
74:| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
75:| --- | --- | --- | --- |
76:| `seconds` | number | Required | How long to record, from 1 to 600 seconds. It's wall-clock time, so a [pause](#a-person-can-pause-or-stop-it) shortens what's recorded. |
77:| `source` | `screen`, `voice_over` or `camera` | `screen` | What's recorded. See [Choose a source](#choose-a-source). |
78:
79:### Display or window
80:
81:| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
82:| --- | --- | --- | --- |
83:| `display` | whole number, 0 or more | `0` | Which display, as an index into the displays that can be shared, 0 being the main one. Can't be used with `window`. |
84:| `window` | whole number | None | The id of one window to record on its own, at that window's own size, instead of a display. Can't be used with `display`. |
85:| `include_framejob_windows` | boolean | `false` | Puts Frame Job's own windows, the editor and the preview, in a display recording. By default they're left out. With `window` it changes nothing. Frame Job's own sound stays out either way. |
86:| `size` | `nominal` or `best`, in any case | `nominal` | `nominal` records a display's point size, and `best` its pixel size, twice the points on a Retina display. An odd dimension is rounded up to even. |
87:| `rate` | `30` or `60` | `60` | The most frames a second the file may hold, and the canvas rate of a new project the recording opens as. |
88:
89:A screen recording's frame rate is whatever the screen did, because a frame arrives only when something changes. A mostly still screen reports a low, fractional rate. That's the file and not a fault, and the picture holds its last frame to the end of the so
90:
91:### Sound
92:
93:| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
94:| --- | --- | --- | --- |
95:| `system_audio` | boolean | `true` | Records what the Mac plays as the movie's one stereo 48 kHz track. It takes in every app but Frame Job, so the timeline can play meanwhile and stay out of it. `false` writes a movie with no audio track, and `has_audio` 
96:| `microphone` | boolean | `false` | Also records the default microphone, to a second file beside the movie named `<movie name> (Microphone).m4a`. |
97:
98:The microphone's file lands as its own clip on a new track at the back named **Microphone**, lined up with the picture by the measured `mic_offset`. When the microphone began first and there's no room for it there, the clip's head is trimmed rather than the
99:
100:A microphone that fails doesn't fail the recording. The picture lands, that stretch has no `mic_path`, and `mic_problem` and the note say why. See [System audio and the microphone](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/).
101:
102:### Pointer and keys
103:
104:| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
105:| --- | --- | --- | --- |
106:| `cursor` | `separate` or `in_picture` | `separate` | `separate` keeps the pointer out of the movie, and Frame Job draws it on the clip from the cursor file, where you can restyle it. `in_picture` has macOS burn the pointer into the movie. |
107:| `show_clicks` | boolean | `false` | Shows each mouse click. With `in_picture`, a circle is drawn around each click into the movie. With `separate`, the clips land with click ripples on, drawn by Frame Job. |
108:| `keys` | `off` or `shortcuts` | `off` | `shortcuts` writes keyboard shortcuts into the cursor files, and needs the Input Monitoring permission. |
109:
110:Every display or window recording writes a cursor file beside each movie, named `<movie name>.fjcursor`, holding the pointer's path, its clicks and scrolls. A problem with it never fails the recording. `segments` reports it as `cursor_problem`, and the not
111:
112:With `keys: "shortcuts"`, the file records each shortcut pressed with ⌘ or ⌃, or with ⌥ and an arrow, Delete, Forward Delete, Return, Enter, Tab or Esc, spelled like `cmd+shift+4`. Every other key is a mark of the time alone, never which key was typed. Not
113:
114:### Where it goes
115:
116:| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
117:| --- | --- | --- | --- |
118:| `path` | string | `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings` | A folder to record into, created if it doesn't exist. It names the folder and never the file, and the answer's `path` is the file that was written. A blank string means the default folder. |
119:| `project` | string | The front project | The open project to land in, as `get_project` reports its path. One that names nothing open is refused, and it never turns into a new project. |
120:| `place` | boolean | `true` | Puts clips on the timeline, in one undo step with the media. `false` adds the recording to the media list only, and the note says to place it with `add_clip`. |
121:
122:In a new project `place: false` has no effect, because the picture is the document. Its clips are on the timeline, one for each stretch and the first at 0, and the note says so.
123:
124:## Record a voice-over
125:
126:`source: "voice_over"` records the default microphone alone, as the panel's **Microphone Only** does. `microphone: true` is implied. The only permission it reads is the Microphone one, and it looks nothing up.
127:
128:Each stretch between pauses is its own `.m4a` file. The files land touching, from the playhead, on one new track at the back named **Microphone**, in one undo step, **Add Recording**. In a new project the first file is the document, 1920 × 1080 at `rate`, 
129:
130:The answer's `path` is the first `.m4a`, its `width` and `height` are 0, and it has no `mic_path`. A microphone that stops on its own ends the voice-over, what it wrote lands, and `mic_problem` and the note say so.
131:
132:See [Record a voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/).
133:
134:## Record a camera alone
135:
136:`source: "camera"` records one camera, with no screen, and lands it as a screen recording's picture lands. It reads the Camera permission and never the Screen Recording one. `microphone: true` adds the default microphone as a second file, as for a screen.
137:
138:Recording starts once the camera has settled at its frame rate, which takes up to a second, and `seconds` counts from its first frame. While it runs, a recorder panel left open with a camera chosen reads "The camera is recording." in its preview. The movie

input.new_string:
`record_screen` can run the same steps, through its `camera_cutout`, `enhance`, `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing` arguments, with some differences:

- Every step is off unless the agent asks for it, **Zoom in on clicks** included.
- Every step needs the recording placed on the timeline, so none works with `place: false`.
- `enhance` needs `microphone: true` or a voice-over.
- `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing` need `keys: "shortcuts"`.
- `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing` can't be used with a voice-over or a camera on its own.
- Enhance Voice runs at −16 LUFS, not at the Normalize row's target. The agent can call `enhance_voice` afterwards for another target.
- The other steps use the tools' own defaults, never the values a sheet remembers.
- A speed-up that leaves a clip silent above ×12 is applied, and the agent is told.

The call's answer holds each step's own answer, or a sentence under `enhance_error`, `auto_zoom_error` and so on when the step couldn't run. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/#run-steps-after-it-lands).
